full: deep seek went down last night. Yours didn't have to. You just watched its status page log four hours and fifty-two minutes of downtime. You chat with deep seek in the browser, or you call its A P I from your side projects. Either way, it feels like one thing. Somewhere along the way, the website became the model. deep seek is two things stacked. The model is files of numbers, called its parameters. The service is someone else's computers running those files for you. Last night, that service went dark. The files did not change. One of those two things can live on your disk. Treat the chat app like a streaming service. The G G U F file, a single file holding a whole model, is the disc on your shelf. The service going dark does not touch the disc. deep seek published the R one weights, the trained model files themselves, free for anyone under the M I T license. They sit on Hugging Face right now. L M studio or llama.cpp runs the file on your machine. No account, no A P I key, no status page to check. Now the honest part. At the common download quality, the full deep seek R one is a four hundred four gigabyte file. Your gaming PC is not loading that. Neither is your Mac. deep seek also shipped distills, smaller models trained to imitate the big one. One of those carries seven billion parameters. un-sloth's G G U F card sizes it against a twenty-four gigabyte gaming GPU, an R T X forty ninety for example. One catch. A disc holds the identical movie. Your copy is cut down, so the quality genuinely drops. When you need the full model's best answers, the cloud is still where that brain lives. The A P I was never the model. A file on your disk has no status page.
